heard: A structure 3 billion light years long should not exist. In 2021, student Alexia Lopez was mapping distant light in the constellation Boaodes. She analyzed magnesium-2 absorption lines, using ultra-bright quasars as giant lamps to illuminate hidden matter. Using the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, Lopez found a colossal crescent of galaxies stretching 3.3 billion light years across. This giant arc is so massive, it spans 115th the radius of the entire observable universe. Standard cosmology says gravity cannot form structures larger than 1.2 billion light years. There simply hasn't been enough time since the Big Bang for something this big to clump together. This gargantuan galaxy cluster suggests that our basic understanding of the universe is actually broken.
